issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who fails to complete a commercial sale of immovable property by an expressly essential deadline may be denied specific performance when the contract permits termination for that failure.
material_facts: The purchaser, which was engaged in building construction, agreed to buy land for a commercial transaction.

The agreement expressly made time essential, set a one-year period for completion, and provided for cancellation and return of the earnest money if the purchaser failed to complete within that period.
The purchaser was responsible for obtaining clearance for part of the land but failed to obtain it within the agreed period.
There was no evidence that the vendor delayed signing necessary applications or petitions.
After the deadline, the vendor cancelled the agreement and sent the earnest money back by cheque, which the purchaser refused to accept.
issues.conclusion: The vendor was entitled to terminate the contract, and the purchaser was not entitled to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a defendant may raise a defence available under contract law; Section 55 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 makes a contract voidable at the promisee's option when a party fails to perform by the specified time and the parties intended time to be essential. Although time is not normally of the essence in contracts for the sale of immovable property, it may be essential where the agreement clearly says so, the transaction is commercial, and the other terms do not displace that intention. The Court relied on Jamshed Khodaram Irani v. Burjorji Dhunjibhai, Gomathinayagam Pillai v. Palaniswami Nadar, K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan, Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani, and M/s. Hind Construction Contractors v. State of Maharashtra.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and immovable_property_sale and commercial_transaction and express_essential_deadline and purchaser_failed_deadline and contract_provided_cancellation and not vendor_caused_delay and not terms_negated_deadline

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.immovable_property_sale: The contract concerns the sale of immovable property.
predicates.commercial_transaction: The purchaser entered into the transaction for a commercial purpose.
predicates.express_essential_deadline: The parties expressly agreed that completion by a specified deadline was essential.
predicates.purchaser_failed_deadline: The purchaser failed to complete its required performance by the agreed deadline.
predicates.contract_provided_cancellation: The contract provided for cancellation if the purchaser failed to complete on time.
predicates.vendor_caused_delay: The vendor delayed the purchaser's performance or the steps needed to complete it.
predicates.terms_negated_deadline: Other contract terms displaced the stated intention that the deadline was essential.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeks specific performance of an immovable-property sale made for commercial purposes, the vendor may terminate and specific performance may be denied if the purchaser misses an expressly essential deadline, the contract provides for cancellation, the vendor did not cause the delay, and no other term negates the deadline.

issues.legal_issue: A party seeking discretionary specific performance may be denied relief for materially concealing from the court a fact relevant to the dispute.
material_facts: Before the purchaser filed suit, the vendor sent the earnest money back by account-payee cheque under registered post.
The purchaser refused the cheque before filing suit.
The purchaser's plaint omitted the refusal and represented that the earnest money had not been returned.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser's suppression of the material fact disentitled it to discretionary relief of specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: A party seeking discretionary equitable relief must disclose material facts candidly; material suppression may justify refusing that relief. A fact is material if it matters to determination of the dispute. The Court relied on the clean-hands principle discussed in I.C.F. Spry's Equitable Remedies, including Armstrong v. Sheppard & Short Ltd., and on Arunima Baruah v. Union of India.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.discretionary_relief_sought: The plaintiff asked the court to exercise discretion to grant equitable relief.
predicates.plaintiff_suppressed_material_fact: The plaintiff concealed a fact relevant to determining the dispute.

issues.definition: A plaintiff seeking discretionary specific performance may be denied that relief when the plaintiff conceals a fact relevant to the dispute.
